Further, a handler that merely checks draining and queues cannot prove all queued persistence has completed before workflow completion. State resume ordering from that acknowledged queue.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The common thesis — disk projection is the authoritative read source; Temporal is the write-ahead log — is correct and already materially shipped (makeReadsDiskAuthoritative returns on-disk projection as source-of-truth with a typed workflow_unresponsive advisory; dualWriteAfterMutation writes to both). All three decisions are architecturally sound. (D1) read-only bypass preserves C2 (no second write surface) and does NOT violate the AGENTS.md 'no file-backed runtime' prose because that rule is scoped to RUNTIME/writes, not reads — the design is more precise than the prose. (D2) hibernation via complete-and-recreate is the structurally correct Temporal pattern for bounding running workflow COUNT: continueAsNew only bounds history size not count (Temporal docs), auto-archive is terminal, and a creation-ceiling blocks users. (D3) bounded status probe is consistent with existing worker-free read laws. External evidence confirms signals are replay-safe (query replays history including signal events), so DDC1 is achievable via the existing wf.defineSignal/setHandler infrastructure. Replay-safety and no-simpler-alternative claims hold. Deviations are MINOR: one lever citation name is wrong (pushFinding -> addNonHealthyFinding), three cited rq- requirement IDs do not exist as anchored specs, the C6 in-flight-signal drain sequencing is named as a risk but its mechanism is underspecified, and live outage evidence shows adv_change_show heavy-include reads still time out (bypass coverage should be enumerated).

tradeoffs: Hibernation adds a non-terminal lifecycle state and checkpoint/resume machinery vs. relying on Temporal retention alone (which cannot auto-complete condition-waiting workflows).
Read-only bypass increases read-path branching and advisory-marker surface vs. a single Temporal-sourced read path.
Complete-and-recreate resume pays workflow-start latency on first post-hibernation mutation vs. a warm always-running workflow.
Critical-path probe (3s) adds a real read to every health check vs. an optimistic healthy default (mitigated by the timeout being far under the 9801ms budget).
A new lifecycle state touches adv_change_list visibility, default-list filtering (DONT4), and every consumer of lifecycleState — broader blast radius than a pure read-path change.

alternatives_considered.option: continueAsNew to bound running workflow count
alternatives_considered.rationale: Temporal docs confirm continueAsNew restarts the workflow with carried state to prevent history-limit overflow but the workflow keeps RUNNING — it bounds history size, not running count. Does not achieve the hibernation objective.
Bounds count but blocks users from creating new changes once the ceiling is hit — strictly worse UX than a non-blocking hibernation that auto-resumes on mutation.
Archive is a TERMINAL state; cannot resume. Hibernation exists specifically because a reversible middle state is needed.

alternatives_considered.option: Lazy/on-demand workflow spawning (spawn changeWorkflow only when a mutation arrives, complete immediately after)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would bound running count to currently-mutating changes without a new lifecycle state. Viable and arguably simpler. Tradeoffs: per-mutation workflow-start latency, loss of warm query handlers (reads always fall back to disk-only), and a larger change to the fundamental per-change-workflow model. Hibernation is lower blast-radius; the design should add one paragraph explicitly rejecting lazy-spawn so the simplicity choice is defensible on record.

blocking_findings.label: blocker
blocking_findings.what: Decision 2's draining-flag barrier does not specify a deterministic, durable handoff for signals arriving while hibernation waits or after its queuedSignals verification.
blocking_findings.why: C6 requires safe handling. A Temporal workflow cannot directly write the disk projection; filesystem/network I/O must be an Activity. Further, a handler that merely checks draining and queues cannot prove all queued persistence has completed before workflow completion. Temporal warns that completion may abandon unfinished signal handlers unless allHandlersFinished is awaited. The ADR therefore asserts a critical section without defining the required Activity, idempotency key/ordering, final queue watermark or sealed state, and completion barrier.
blocking_findings.fix: Revise Decision 2 to define a replay-safe durable drain protocol: workflow-owned sequence/epoch, Activity-backed idempotent projection append, durable acknowledgement for every pre-seal signal, await allHandlersFinished (or explicitly typed rejection), a final sealed/watermark step, and only then completion. State resume ordering from that acknowledged queue.

# Resolve ADV persistence recovery architecture

## Why

ADV's persistence layer (Temporal + disk projection) has become a structural regression generator. Each fix creates the conditions for the next failure. Three architectural decisions — no existing change frames them — will determine whether the layer stabilizes or continues the spiral.

Today's operational evidence (2026-08-04): 128 active changes with 191 running workflows; bulk-closing 74 stale changes reduced the active list but not the running workflow count; `adv_status` health view still times out despite the store/tool/retry bounding shipped in `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead`; `adv_doctor` reports healthy while reads time out.

## What this change must decide (not implement)

### Decision 1 — Out-of-band recovery bypass

Accept a read-only out-of-band recovery surface so ADV can read/diagnose/record when Temporal+disk-projection are down, explicitly superseding the "no file-backed runtime" rule's scope. OR formally accept total-layer-outage = total-ADV-outage as a documented design boundary.

### Decision 2 — Workflow hibernation (projection-as-primary with Temporal-as-write-ahead)

Accept hibernation as the implementation direction: stale changes checkpoint to disk and terminate their workflows, freeing Temporal resources. Resume re-creates the workflow from the checkpoint. The foundations are already shipped (`makeReadsDiskAuthoritative`, `gateMutationSuccessDisk`, `makeToolReadsWorkerFree`).

### Decision 3 — Diagnostic trustworthiness

Require health probes to exercise the critical read path (fail when `adv_status` can't return within budget) rather than report server/worker liveness. OR accept that `adv_doctor` and `adv_status view:"health"` measure different things and document the distinction.

## User Outcomes

- [ ] ADV remains operational when the Temporal layer degrades (Decision 1)
- [ ] Running workflow count stays bounded to recently-active changes; stale changes are reclaimable without data loss (Decision 2)
- [ ] Health diagnostics accurately reflect whether the system can actually serve reads (Decision 3)
- [ ] Discovery will firm acceptance criteria and success criteria for each decision

## Affected Code

This is an ADR-shaped decision change. Implementation is downstream:

- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/` — hibernation lifecycle, resume-from-checkpoint
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts` — hibernation signal handler, checkpoint emission
- `plugin/src/tools/` — doctor integration for automatic hibernation, health probe trustworthiness
- `plugin/src/plugin-init.ts` — out-of-band recovery surface (Decision 1)
- `AGENTS.md` — supersede "no file-backed runtime" rule scope if Decision 1 is affirmative

## Constraints

- No data loss. Hibernation must preserve all change state.
- No second parallel deadline mechanism (DONT3 from existing constraints).
- Worker-bundle determinism must not be affected (workflows.ts changes are replay-sensitive).
- The ADR must be approved at the design gate before implementation begins.

## Impact

- **Decision 1:** Supersedes a standing architectural rule. Enables ADV to self-diagnose during layer outages.
- **Decision 2:** Adds a lifecycle state (`hibernated`). Changes how `adv_change_list` defaults work. Enables automatic resource reclamation.
- **Decision 3:** May change what `adv_doctor` reports as "healthy." Makes diagnostics actionable.

## Risks

- Hibernation + resume adds a workflow-recreation path that must be deterministic (Temporal replay safety).
- Out-of-band bypass creates a second read surface that must stay consistent with Temporal-backed reads.
- Diagnostic changes may surface latent issues that were previously masked by false-healthy reports.

## Validation Plan

- Decision artifacts reviewed at design gate with user approval
- Each affirmative decision produces a downstream implementation change with its own TDD validation
- This change itself produces an ADR-class artifact (design.md) recording the decisions and their rationale
documents.problemStatement:
## Problem Statement

ADV made Temporal-plus-disk-projection the sole persistence path for its own operational state, with no out-of-band recovery bypass. When that layer degrades, ADV cannot even record the defect — observed directly 2026-08-02 when `adv_change_create` to log a read-timeout defect itself timed out. Separately, the persistence/projection layer regenerates regressions faster than they're fixed: `fixMultiSessionConcurrency` (Jul 29) created the per-session worker sprawl that produced today's `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead`. Each fix is a link in a spiral, and no change asks whether the layer is structurally a regression generator.

This change owns three architectural decisions that no existing change frames. It is an ADR-shaped decision change, not an implementation change. Downstream implementation is gated on these decisions.

### Updated evidence (2026-08-04, post `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead` ship + bulk cleanup)

The original evidence from 2026-08-02 is now corroborated and enriched by today's operational findings:

- **Workflow accumulation is structural.** This project had 128 active changes and 191 running Temporal workflows across 15 projects. Bulk-closing 74 stale changes reduced the active list to 54 but **did not reduce the running workflow count** — each change's workflow persists independently of its lifecycle status. There is no mechanism to reclaim Temporal resources from stale, non-terminal changes.
- **The foundations for hibernation already shipped.** `makeReadsDiskAuthoritative` (archived 2026-07-23) made the disk projection the authoritative read source with workflow queries as enrichment-only + circuit-broken. `gateMutationSuccessDisk` made mutations require disk-projection confirmation. `makeToolReadsWorkerFree` made reads not require the Temporal worker. Reads already serve correctly from disk when the workflow is unavailable.
- **3 of 4 `adv_status` views now return typed degraded output within the host cap** after `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead`. The `health` view still times out — its health executor has an unbounded path that the enrichment-layer fix didn't cover (`fixHealthViewTimeoutHealth` created to investigate). This is itself evidence that per-workflow probing doesn't scale.
- **The "no file-backed runtime" rule now blocks recovery.** When every Temporal-backed tool exceeds the 10s host cap, ADV cannot create a change, close a change, or record the defect. The recovery machinery depends on the thing it recovers.

## Decision gap 1 — No out-of-band recovery bypass

| Layer | Finding |
|---|---|
| Architectural rule | `AGENTS.md`: "Runtime change/task/gate state uses Temporal-only persistence… do not restore a legacy SQLite/file-backed runtime path." |
| Consequence | Every ADV operation — read, write, recover, govern, record-a-defect — round-trips Temporal/disk-projection. |
| Observed failure | 2026-08-02: all Temporal-backed tools exceeded 10s host cap; `adv_change_create` to log the defect timed out. 2026-08-04: `adv_change_close` on 74 stale changes wrote projections but failed postcondition verification because the Temporal workflow describe timed out. |
| Coverage check | `enforceTemporalOperation` makes the path safe but keeps Temporal as source of truth. `hardenProjectionHydration` keeps disk projection as the ADV-internal read path, not a recovery escape hatch. Neither adds a bypass. |

The "no file-backed runtime" rule is now the thing making the system unrecoverable under total layer outage. This rule was written to prevent a *specific* legacy regression; it was not written to forbid a read-only out-of-band *recovery* surface. The two are being conflated.

**Decision:** Accept a read-only out-of-band recovery surface (ADV can read/diagnose/record when Temporal+disk-projection are down), explicitly superseding the "no file-backed runtime" rule's scope — OR formally accept total-layer-outage = total-ADV-outage as a documented design boundary with the operational consequences made explicit.

## Decision gap 2 — Workflow hibernation: projection-as-primary with Temporal-as-write-ahead

The persistence/projection layer is a regression generator. Direct evidence (two links of the spiral):

```
fixMultiSessionConcurrency (2026-07-29, archived)
  RCA: worker_singleton_enforce declared false but resolved true → peer sessions lacked pollers
  Fix:  guarantee each session its own worker + queue
  Side effect (by design): 9 concurrent workers/project
    ↓
2026-08-02 saturation: query throughput starves under 9 pollers
    ↓
fixMultiSessionTemporalRead (2026-08-02 → 2026-08-04, archived)
  Bounded store, tool, retry, enrichment layers
  Fixed 3/4 views; health view still times out
    ↓
fixHealthViewTimeoutHealth (2026-08-04, created)
  Health executor has unbounded path not covered by the read-bounding fix
```

The layer that was fixed became the layer that broke. No change asks: is the per-session-worker + per-session-queue + Temporal-query-for-every-read design's regression rate acceptable, or does the layer need simplification?

**Proposed direction: Workflow Hibernation.** Given that the foundations are already shipped (disk-authoritative reads, disk-gated mutations, worker-free reads), the natural next step is a lifecycle policy that uses them:

```
active → hibernated → active (resume)
              ↓
          archived (terminal)
```

**Hibernation** (triggered by staleness threshold or workflow-count ceiling):
1. Verify disk projection is complete and authoritative (already enforced by `gateMutationSuccessDisk`)
2. Terminate the Temporal workflow (frees resources immediately)
3. Change lifecycle state → `hibernated`
4. Active list excludes hibernated changes by default → fast enumeration

**Cold reads** (already supported via `makeReadsDiskAuthoritative`):
- `adv_change_show` serves from disk projection
- `adv_change_list` excludes hibernated by default; `status: "hibernated"` shows them
- Default list shows only non-hibernated → bounded workflow enumeration

**Resume** (when a hibernated change is accessed for mutation):
1. Check disk projection exists and is valid
2. Re-create the workflow seeded with the checkpointed state
3. Change lifecycle state → `active`
4. Mutation proceeds normally

**Automatic hibernation** (doctor integration):
- `adv_doctor` detects changes with `lastActivityAt > N days ago` that have running workflows
- Hibernates them (or proposes hibernation if below a safety threshold)
- Also detects when running workflow count exceeds a ceiling and hibernates the stalest

This would keep the running workflow count bounded to recently-active changes, make ADV reads fast without per-workflow enumeration, and preserve all change data in durable disk projections.

**Decision:** Accept hibernation as the implementation direction for Decision 2 (projection-as-primary with Temporal-as-write-ahead), and create the implementation change — OR formally reject it and continue per-symptom ticketing.

## Decision gap 3 — Diagnostic trustworthiness

Health probes report liveness, not critical-path health. Today `adv_doctor` returned `healthy` (server_alive: true, worker_alive: true, queue_serviceable: true) while `adv_status view:"health"` timed out at the 10s host cap. The health executor's deep probes hang even though the worker is running and the store read path works.

**Decision:** Health probes must exercise the critical read path (fail when `adv_status` can't return within budget) rather than report server/worker liveness — OR accept that `adv_doctor` and `adv_status view:"health"` measure different things and document the distinction.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the bypass (downstream change, post-decision).
- Implementing hibernation (downstream implementation change, post-decision).
- The budget/degradation work already owned by `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead` (archived) and `fixHealthViewTimeoutHealth` (created).
- Per-project stale-workflow cleanup (cross-project ops concern).

## Decision authority

This change requires design-gate user approval (architectural tradeoff) and should produce an ADR-class artifact superseding the relevant scope of the standing "no file-backed runtime" rule if Decisions 1 and/or 2 are affirmative.

## Foundation changes already shipped (provenance for the implementation direction)

| Change | What it shipped | How hibernation uses it |
|---|---|---|
| `makeReadsDiskAuthoritative` (archived) | Disk projection = read source of truth; workflow query = enrichment-only + circuit-broken | Cold reads already work when workflow is terminated |
| `gateMutationSuccessDisk` (closed) | Mutations require disk-projection confirmation | Disk projection is guaranteed authoritative before hibernation |
| `makeToolReadsWorkerFree` (closed) | Reads don't require the Temporal worker | Hibernated reads need no worker |
| `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead` (archived) | Bounded store/tool/retry/enrichment read paths | Proves reads return within budget even under load |
| `addDependencyAwareResume` (archived) | Resume mechanism with dependency tracking | Hibernation resume can leverage this |

# Agreement

> **Scope revision (2026-08-04).** This agreement originally covered three decisions. Decision 2
> (workflow hibernation) was split to change `decideWorkflowHibernation` after five independent
> structural review rounds each found a different D2 foundation assumption that did not survive
> verification; Decisions 1 and 3 passed clean in all five rounds. Split approved by the user.
>
> **Items are renumbered sequentially** to match the minted contract, which derives IDs
> positionally. Mapping from the pre-split agreement:
>
> | Pre-split | Now | Item |
> |---|---|---|
> | AC1 | **AC1** | read-only out-of-band recovery surface |
> | AC3 | **AC2** | health probes exercise the critical read path |
> | AC4 | **AC3** | foundation-change provenance |
> | C2 | **C1** | no second parallel write surface |
> | C3 | **C2** | preserve Temporal replay safety |
> | C4 | **C3** | ADR approved at design gate before implementation |
> | SC1-3, DONT1-3 | unchanged | — |
>
> Moved to `decideWorkflowHibernation`: pre-split **AC2, AC5, C1, C5, C6, DONT4**, and
> Objective 2.

## Objectives

1. Resolve whether ADV needs an out-of-band read-only recovery surface to remain operational
   during Temporal layer outages (Decision 1)
2. Resolve whether health diagnostics must exercise the critical read path rather than report
   server/worker liveness (Decision 3)

## Success Criteria

1. The ADR artifact documents each decision with rationale, alternatives considered, and consequences
2. Each affirmative decision has a clear path to a downstream implementation change
3. The decisions collectively address the regression-spiral root cause, not just symptoms

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given the evidence of ADV becoming non-operational during Temporal outages (2026-08-02, 2026-08-04), when Decision 1 is resolved, then the decision establishes a read-only out-of-band recovery surface, with limited write deferred to an explicit follow-up.
2. Given the evidence of `adv_doctor` reporting healthy while `adv_status view:"health"` times out (2026-08-04), when Decision 3 is resolved, then the decision requires health probes to exercise the critical read path.
3. Evidence: ADR foundation-change provenance verified by review of archived change records (`makeReadsDiskAuthoritative`, `gateMutationSuccessDisk`, `makeToolReadsWorkerFree`, `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead`).

## Constraints

1. Must not introduce a second parallel write surface (bypass is read-only initially; limited write is follow-up)
2. Must preserve Temporal workflow replay safety for any workflow code changes
3. The ADR must be approved at the design gate before implementation begins

## Avoidances

1. Do not implement in this change — it is decision-only
2. Do not defer the decisions by creating more per-symptom tickets
3. Do not conflate "no file-backed runtime" (legacy prevention) with "no out-of-band read" (recovery prevention)

## Preview Applicability

`visual_surface: false` — internal ADV lifecycle/architecture, no browser-visible surface.
`preview_expectation`: `exact_route_required: not_applicable`,
`data_state_expectation: not_applicable`, `viewport_expectation: not_applicable`.

## Decisions

### User Decisions

1. **Bypass scope (D1):** Read-only initially; limited write deferred to an explicit follow-up.
   Read-only is safe (no dual-write conflicts). Limited write enables self-repair but adds a
   dual-write surface needing reconciliation — worth doing but not in the first implementation.

2. **Scope split (2026-08-04):** Decision 2 split to its own change. Rationale: five review
   rounds, five blockers, all in D2. The recurring failure was the design asserting that an
   existing ADV mechanism already guaranteed a property it did not — three consecutive rounds
   against three different mechanisms. D2's preconditions were never firmed at discovery, so
   design kept reaching for whatever looked adjacent. D1 and D3 are decision-ready; D2 is not.

### Agent Decisions (LBP)

1. **Diagnostic critical path (D3):** The doctor's health check should include a bounded
   `adv_status view:"summary"` invocation. If it times out, doctor reports degraded. This
   directly exercises the read path the user cares about.

2. **Durability vocabulary (carried from the D2 review, retained because D1 depends on it):**
   `dualWriteAfterMutation` (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:364`) is a best-effort
   cache-refresh path and is not a durability guarantee; `assertDurablePersist`
   (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/disk-persist.ts:44`) is the durability gate. Decision 1's
   staleness marker (DDC4) exists because the former may silently skip.

*(The pre-split Agent Decision 2 — persist queued signals to the disk projection and replay on
resume — was overturned at design: Temporal workflow code cannot perform filesystem I/O. It moved
to `decideWorkflowHibernation` as a ruled-out mechanism.)*

## Deferred Questions

1. **Limited write bypass** — deferred to a follow-up change per user decision. The initial

# Design — ADV Persistence Recovery Architecture (ADR)

> **Scope note (2026-08-04):** this ADR originally carried three decisions. Decision 2 (workflow
> hibernation) was split to `decideWorkflowHibernation` after five structural review rounds each
> found a different D2 foundation assumption that did not survive verification. Decisions 1 and 3
> passed clean in all rounds and are the scope of this change.

## Architecture Overview

Decision-only ADR resolving two questions about ADV's persistence layer. No code is written here;
each affirmative decision produces a downstream implementation change.

Shared thesis: **the disk projection is already the authoritative read source; Temporal is the
write-ahead log. The recovery and diagnostic surfaces should reflect this.**

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ┌─────────────┐    write     ┌──────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ ADV Tools   │─────────────▶│ Temporal Workflow (WAL)  │   │
│  │             │              └──────────┬───────────────┘   │
│  │             │    read                 │ dual-write         │
│  │             │◀────────────────────────│                     │
│  │             │    read (fallback)      ▼                     │
│  │             │◀────────────────┌──────────────────┐         │
│  │             │                 │ Disk Projection  │         │
│  └─────────────┘                 │ (authoritative)  │         │
│                                  └──────────────────┘         │
│  D1: disk projection serves reads even when WAL is down      │
│  D3: doctor exercises the read path, not just WAL liveness   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Persistence-boundary invariant:** all durable I/O happens **host-side**, in the store layer,
never inside workflow code. Temporal workflow code is deterministic-replay code and may not
perform filesystem or network I/O directly.

**Two distinct host-side write paths — do not conflate them.** An earlier draft did, producing a
false durability claim. The distinction is retained because D1 depends on it directly: DDC4's
staleness marker exists precisely because the first path may silently skip, and D1's Correctness
consequence is stated against that fact.

| Path | Anchor | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `dualWriteAfterMutation` | `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:364` | **Best-effort cache refresh.** Labeled "Best-effort by design: this is a cache-refresh path" (`:411`). Skips the disk write when the post-mutation readback is not `confirmed` (`:399`), returns no value (`:405`), or the workflow is known-poisoned (`:366`). A convergence optimization, **not** a durability guarantee. |
| `assertDurablePersist` / `DiskPersistOutcome` | `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/disk-persist.ts:70` (gate), `:31` (outcome union), `:44` (typed error) | **The durability gate.** From `gateMutationSuccessDisk`: classifies the atomic `change.json` write as `persisted` / `skipped` / `failed`, and throws `DiskProjectionPersistError` on failure so a mutation cannot report success while absent from every disk-first reader. |

## Decision 1 — Read-only out-of-band recovery surface

**Verdict: AFFIRMATIVE (read-only initially; limited write deferred)**

**Lever:** `makeReadsDiskAuthoritative` (archived; implementation commit `1879fb64`) already made
the disk projection the read source of truth, with workflow queries enrichment-only and
circuit-broken. The bypass extends this to serve reads when Temporal is completely unreachable —
not merely slow. The projection it reads is kept honest by `assertDurablePersist`
(`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/disk-persist.ts:70`) on the mutation path, and
opportunistically refreshed by `dualWriteAfterMutation` (`index.ts:364`).

**Read tools covered:** `adv_change_show` (all include flags — snapshot, ledger, readyTasks,
subagentReports, briefingPacket), `adv_change_list`, `adv_status` (all four views),
`adv_task_show` / `adv_task_list` / `adv_task_ready`, `adv_doctor`.

Live evidence (2026-08-04): heavy `adv_change_show` includes time out at 10s during a Temporal
outage even with the disk fallback, because the fallback still attempts a Temporal describe
first. The bypass skips that attempt entirely.

**What the bypass means concretely:**
- When the Temporal client cannot connect (refused, timeout, server down), reads fall back to the
  disk projection carrying `_advisory.source: "disk-only-out-of-band"` (DDC4)
- Mutations are not attempted — `adv_change_create`, `adv_task_update`, `adv_gate_complete`
  return typed `RECOVERY_MODE_READ_ONLY` instead of timing out
- Activates automatically when Temporal health checks fail; deactivates on recovery

**Why read-only, not read+write:**
- Read-only carries zero dual-write risk — the disk projection is already authoritative for reads
- Write during outage needs reconciliation (what if Temporal recovers with different state?) —
  that is the deferred follow-up
- The "no file-backed runtime" rule (`AGENTS.md`, Scope and entry points) is superseded for the
  read-only recovery scope only; its original intent (blocking legacy SQLite/file-backed
  *mutation* paths) is preserved

**Alternatives considered:**
- *Read+write bypass with reconciliation* — enables self-repair but adds a dual-write surface;
  deferred
- *Accept total outage as a design boundary* — operationally unacceptable; ADV must stay
  diagnostic during its own layer's outages
- *External recovery CLI* — adds operational burden; the bypass should be automatic

**Consequences:**
- *Operational:* ADV stays readable and diagnosable during a total Temporal outage. Incident
  response no longer needs Temporal up to answer "what state is this change in?"
- *Compatibility:* Additive. Normal reads unchanged; only the total-unreachable branch is new.
  Consumers ignoring `_advisory` keep working.
- *Correctness:* Bypass reads may be stale relative to an in-flight mutation, because
  `dualWriteAfterMutation` is best-effort and may have skipped the refresh. Every bypass read is
  therefore marked (DDC4) and must not be treated as authoritative for gate decisions.
- *Failure mode:* Mutations fail fast and typed rather than hanging to the 10s tool timeout,
  converting an unclassified timeout into an actionable error.
- *Cost:* A health-state branch in the read path plus an `AGENTS.md` rule-scope amendment. The
  deferred write path remains an open, accepted gap.

**AGENTS.md amendment scope:** existing rule — "Runtime change/task/gate state uses Temporal-only
persistence… do not restore a legacy SQLite/file-backed runtime path." Superseded scope —
"…except for a read-only out-of-band recovery surface that serves existing disk projections when
Temporal is unreachable. No mutation path may bypass Temporal."

## Decision 3 — Diagnostic trustworthiness

**Verdict: AFFIRMATIVE (critical-path exercising)**

**Lever:** `plugin/src/tools/doctor.ts:72-84` defines `DoctorFindingClass` (`healthy`,
`degraded`, `unhealthy`); `addNonHealthyFinding` (`:358`) supersedes the optimistic `healthy`
finding when a real issue is detected. The doctor currently checks `server_alive`, `worker_alive`,
`queue_serviceable` — none of which exercise the critical read path.

**What "critical-path exercising" means:**
- Add a bounded `adv_status view:"summary"` probe (3s, per DDC3) to the check sequence
- Returns within budget → read path healthy
- Times out or errors → `addNonHealthyFinding` supersedes `healthy` with
  `degraded: "critical read path timed out"`, and the overall verdict follows

**Why not just improve the existing probes:** `server_alive` checks gRPC connectivity and passes
while the query path is saturated; `worker_alive` checks poller presence and passes while queries
time out under load; `queue_serviceable` checks task-queue reachability and passes while
visibility scans crawl. None touch the user-facing read path.

**Probe overhead (EC7):** one bounded call per doctor run, periodic rather than per-request. Its
3s timeout is well under `STATUS_READ_DEADLINE_BUDGET_MS` (`plugin/src/utils/tool-budgets.ts:31-32`,
derived as `DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS - TOOL_RESPONSE_HEADROOM_MS` = 9801ms), so it fails fast
before contributing meaningfully to saturation.

**Alternatives considered:**
- *Separate health-check tool* — adds operational burden
- *Accept that doctor and health-view measure different things* — leaves the false-healthy gap open
- *Remove the doctor's optimistic default* — broad behavior change; the targeted probe is narrower

**Consequences:**
- *Operational:* Closes the false-healthy gap. The doctor's verdict becomes trustworthy as a
  go/no-go signal — which is why D3 ships first.
- *Compatibility:* Existing findings and classes unchanged; one finding added. Verdicts previously
  reported `healthy` will now sometimes read `degraded` — the intended change, not a regression.
- *Correctness:* Measures the real read path rather than a proxy. Cannot report healthy while
  reads are unusable.
- *Failure mode:* A probe timeout degrades the verdict; it never fails the doctor run. A degraded
  verdict on a transiently-slow host is a tolerated false-negative, preferable to today's
  false-positive.
- *Cost:* ~31% of a single read budget worst-case, on the periodic doctor path only.

**Reproduced during this change's own recovery (2026-08-04):** while recovering from the
doom-loop brick described below, `adv_doctor` reported `healthy: true` with `server_alive`,
`worker_alive`, and `queue_serviceable` all true, while `adv_task_show` timed out at 10s. The
defect D3 addresses demonstrated itself live, against this change. Corroborating evidence from an
unplanned observation, not a purpose-built demonstration.

## ADR Drafts

**ADR-001: Read-only out-of-band recovery surface.** *Status:* Proposed. *Context:* the "no
file-backed runtime" rule blocks recovery during Temporal outages; it was written to prevent
legacy SQLite mutation paths, not read-only recovery. *Decision:* accept a read-only out-of-band
recovery surface; supersede the rule's scope for reads only; no mutation path may bypass Temporal.
*Consequences:* ADV stays diagnostic during outages; limited write deferred; no dual-write risk;
bypass reads carry a staleness marker; outage-time mutations fail typed rather than hanging.

**ADR-003: Critical-path health diagnostics.** *Status:* Proposed. *Context:* `adv_doctor`
reported healthy while `adv_status view:"health"` timed out (2026-08-04, reproduced during this
change's incident recovery); existing probes measure liveness, never the read path. *Decision:*
add a bounded 3s `adv_status view:"summary"` probe routed through `addNonHealthyFinding`.
*Consequences:* verdicts become trustworthy for rollout gating; some previously-healthy verdicts
become `degraded`, as intended; bounded per-run cost, failing fast inside the read budget.

> ADR-002 (workflow hibernation lifecycle) moved to `decideWorkflowHibernation`.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **D3** — no dependencies, smallest scope. Add the critical-path probe. Ship first so health
   reporting is trustworthy for the remaining work.
2. **D1** — extend the disk-projection read path to handle total Temporal unavailability.

Both are independently shippable; neither depends on work outside this change.
`decideWorkflowHibernation` is expected to build on both, but that sequencing is stated there and
is not a commitment of this change.

## LBP Analysis

Both decisions move ADV from "Temporal is the system of record" to "disk projection is the system
of record; Temporal is the write-ahead log" — the standard event-sourcing split, where the event
log is the write-ahead and the materialized view is the read source.

Foundations already shipped (verified against archive commits and test files):
- `makeReadsDiskAuthoritative` (archive `2ac4ceeb`; impl `1879fb64`;
  `convergent-read-disk-authoritative.test.ts`) — disk projection as read source of truth with
  circuit breaker
- `gateMutationSuccessDisk` (archive `f0277b29`;
  `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/disk-persist.ts`) — mutations require a confirmed disk write
- `makeToolReadsWorkerFree` (archive `5a2e0d94`; `change.worker-free.test.ts`) — reads do not
  require the worker
- `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead` (archive `b0294359`) — reads bounded within host cap

## Affected Components

| Component | Decision | Change type | Lever |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:364` | D1 | Read-path bypass; cache convergence (best-effort — not a durability basis) | `dualWriteAfterMutation` |
| `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/disk-persist.ts:70,31,44` | D1 | Durability gate keeping the bypass-read projection honest | `assertDurablePersist` (`:70`), `DiskPersistOutcome` (`:31`), `DiskProjectionPersistError` (`:44`) |
| `plugin/src/tools/doctor.ts:72-84,358` | D3 | Critical-path probe added to findings | `DoctorFindingClass`, `addNonHealthyFinding` |
| `plugin/src/utils/tool-budgets.ts:31-32` | D3 | Probe timeout must sit under this budget | `STATUS_READ_DEADLINE_BUDGET_MS` |
| `AGENTS.md` (Scope and entry points) | D1 | Rule scope superseded for read-only recovery | Prose rule |
| `plugin/src/plugin-init.ts` | D1 | Bypass activation/deactivation on Temporal health | Init sequence |

## Design-Derived Criteria

- **DDC3:** The critical-path probe timeout (3s) must be shorter than
  `STATUS_READ_DEADLINE_BUDGET_MS` (9801ms) to avoid contributing to saturation.
- **DDC4:** The bypass read path must carry `_advisory.source: "disk-only-out-of-band"` so
  consumers can distinguish bypass reads from normal disk-authoritative reads.

> DDC1, DDC2, DDC5, DDC6, DDC7 were hibernation-specific and moved to `decideWorkflowHibernation`.

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Bypass doesn't cover heavy `adv_change_show` includes (observed 2026-08-04) | Medium | D1 must enumerate and cover ALL read tools and include-flag paths, not just summary reads |
| Bypass reads serve stale data during active mutation | Low | Staleness marker (DDC4); bypass reads are never gate-authoritative |
| Critical-path probe amplifies saturation (EC7) | Low | 3s timeout << 9801ms budget; fails fast |
| Bypass masks a real outage by making things "look fine" | Low | D3 ships first; a degraded verdict surfaces the outage even while bypass reads succeed |

## Validator Result

One architecture validation plus six independent structural reviews. Recorded in full rather than
smoothed over, because the pattern is the finding: **every pre-split blocker was in Decision 2**,
each a foundation assumption that did not survive verification. D1 and D3 passed unchanged
throughout. That asymmetry is why D2 was split out.

Contract IDs were renumbered by the post-split re-mint (pre-split AC3→AC2, AC4→AC3, C2→C1,
C3→C2, C4→C3). Rounds below reference **pre-split** IDs.

| Round | Agent | Verdict | Finding |

# Executive Summary — Resolve ADV persistence recovery architecture

## What this delivers

Two architectural decisions, recorded and justified, about how ADV behaves when its own storage
layer is unhealthy. No code ships here — this change exists to decide, so the implementation work
that follows is unambiguous.

**Decision 1 — ADV stays readable during a storage outage.** Today, when Temporal is unreachable,
ADV goes dark: you cannot see what state a change is in, precisely when you most need to. The
decision accepts a read-only recovery surface that serves the existing on-disk copy when Temporal
is down. Reads are marked as potentially stale so nobody mistakes them for authoritative. Writes
are deliberately excluded from this first step — allowing writes during an outage raises
reconciliation questions that deserve their own change.

**Decision 3 — the health check stops lying.** `adv_doctor` currently reports "healthy" by
checking that the server is reachable, the worker is alive, and the queue is serviceable. None of
those touch the path a user actually reads through. The decision requires the doctor to exercise
that real path with a short, bounded probe, and to report `degraded` when it fails.

## Why it matters

These two together change ADV's failure behavior from "silently unusable" to "visibly degraded
but still diagnosable." That is the difference between an outage you can reason about and one you
cannot.

Decision 3 ships first, deliberately: until the health signal is trustworthy, no other rollout in
this area can be judged safe.

## How it was verified

An independent reviewer checked the decision record against the agreed contract and returned
READY. All twelve contract items were confirmed, and a contract review matrix records each one
with its evidence — twelve rows, none failing. Every source reference in the document was checked
to resolve to what it claims, and the four prior changes this work builds on were each verified as
genuinely shipped by locating their archive commits.

The document also passed a check that it contains no implementation — this change was agreed to be
decision-only, and the branch is clean with no commits.

## What changed along the way

The change originally carried a third decision, on workflow hibernation. Five independent review
rounds each found a different assumption in it that did not survive verification — in every case
the design claimed an existing ADV mechanism already guaranteed something it did not. Decisions 1
and 3 passed clean in all five rounds.

Rather than force it through, hibernation was split into its own change,
`decideWorkflowHibernation`, carrying the accumulated analysis: six mechanisms ruled out with
reasons, and the two open questions its discovery must answer. That is a scope correction, not a
deferral — the reviewer assessed it explicitly and agreed.

## Risks and follow-ups

Nothing here is user-visible yet; both decisions still require implementation changes.

Three follow-ups are open:
- **`decideWorkflowHibernation`** — the split-out hibernation decision. ADV still has no way to
  reclaim Temporal resources from stale changes (191 running workflows observed, unaffected by
  closing 74 changes). Unresolved.
- **`clampDoomLoopAccumulator`** — a real ADV defect found during this work. A retry guardrail
  writes a record that ADV's own reader rejects, which can make a change unreadable and
  unwritable. Systemic: any task accumulating four blocked reviews can trigger it. This change hit
  it and was recovered without data loss.
- **Limited-write recovery** — deliberately deferred from Decision 1.

One notable detail: while recovering from that defect, `adv_doctor` reported fully healthy while
a routine read timed out. The problem Decision 3 exists to fix demonstrated itself, unprompted,
during this change's own incident. It is cited as supporting evidence.

## Release Readiness Summary

**Ready to release. Nothing to deploy.**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Code changes | None — decision-only by contract (DONT1) |
| Commits on `change/resolveAdvPersistenceRecovery` | Zero; branch identical to trunk at `5dfcc43` |
| Working trees | Clean (trunk and change worktree) |
| Build / test / lint | Not applicable — no source changed, so no suite is affected |
| Contract review matrix | 12 rows, 0 failing |
| Reviewer verdict | READY (independent `adv-reviewer`, attempt 3) |
| Release blockers | None |

Because no source file changed, the usual quality gates have nothing to act on. Release here means
recording the decisions into the spec history so downstream implementation changes can cite them —
it does not deploy, rebuild, or alter running behavior. No migration, no data impact, no
user-visible change, no rollback plan required.

The three follow-ups above are non-blocking. `clampDoomLoopAccumulator` is the most time-sensitive:
it is a live systemic defect affecting any ADV change, not just this one.

## Bottom line

Two decisions ready to implement, one honestly deferred rather than forced, and one previously
unknown defect found and documented. The decision record is accurate, independently verified, and
carries its full review history — including its own failures — rather than a cleaned-up version.
